mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary or all partners/general partner executing the deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if executed abroad in a Convention State) OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague countries)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or recent extract from foreign trade register for any corporate general partner or corporate limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the partner’s home jurisdiction
Luxembourg Ministry of Justice / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct electronic submission through the RBE portal; apostille not required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of residential address for each individual partner, manager and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, authorized translator, embassy or consulate of the origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification plus Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank seal plus Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered office acceptance letter issued by the licensed domiciliation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Luxembourg-origin document; notarized signature or apostille not required for domestic issuance

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, managers, authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database, United States OFAC SDN List, Luxembourg Ministry of Justice restrictive measures, CSSF/FIU administrative lists and relevant PEP databases. For this Medium_Risk_Enhanced e-commerce jewelry and timepiece business, enhanced due diligence is triggered by PEP status, residence in FATF grey-listed or sanctioned jurisdictions, unusual cross-border payment flows, or use of opaque corporate layers. All screening results must be documented, dated, retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship, and made available to Luxembourg authorities upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Register / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — online electronic filing and search portal at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Luxembourg SCSp must bear a name that is not misleading and that contains the words 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'. The name may be expressed in French, German, Luxembourgish or another language using Latin script; if a non-Latin script is used, a transliteration into French or German must be provided for registration. The name must be sufficiently distinguishable from names already registered in the RCS and must not conflict with protected commercial names or earlier trademarks in Luxembourg or the European Union.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not operate a statutory name-reservation window; availability is tested at filing time. If the RCS rejects the proposed name, the incorporator may immediately submit a revised registration using a new name, or file a formal objection with reasons and supporting trademark/search evidence. A substantive refusal may be appealed before the Luxembourg administrative tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification. Legal representation by a Luxembourg avocat is required for the administrative appeal. No extension of a reservation is available because no reservation is issued; the practical remedy is re-filing with an alternative name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible only through a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent that maintains a physical, staffed address in Luxembourg and files the required legal notice. This is acceptable for RCS registration of an e-commerce jewelry and watches SCSp, provided the company is not carrying on a regulated activity. However, acquiring banks and PSPs such as Stripe or PayPal may reject a purely domiciled vehicle without commercial substance; some form of local substance, such as a dedicated manager, contract counterparties and adequate records, is commercially necessary.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: ≈15% annualized probability of unannounced inspection by the RCS or Luxembourg tax/AML authorities, increasing above 20% where the vehicle uses only a domiciliation agent, has no employees, or presents a disproportionate ledger volume relative to declared substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 101 to 102-5, governing the société en commandite spéciale); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL), under the supervision of the Ministry of Justice
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif et statut de la société en commandite spéciale (constitutive deed / partnership agreement) filed electronically with the RCSL through the MyLBR portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed or paid-up capital is required for an SCSp; contributions are freely fixed in the partnership agreement; no escrow account is legally mandated unless the partners voluntarily impose one
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, acting as the decision-making body of the SCSp and in accordance with the partnership agreement duly adopted, that: (1) the subscriptions of Partners in the initial capital and contribution schedule are hereby approved, allocated as set forth in the contribution statements, with no minimum capital required; (2) the registered office is hereby established at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, as registered address for service and administration; (3) the General Partner and any co-opted natural-person manager are appointed with sole or joint signature authority; (4) the resolution constitutes evidence for registration with Luxembourg Business Registers and RBE, and officers may execute all filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation and verification of company name with Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCSL on-line name query
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an on-line search on the Luxembourg Business Registers availability tool, verify that the name complies with legal requirements and is not misleading, and reserve the chosen name. For an SCSp, the name may include the abbreviation 'SCSp' and must identify at least one general partner. Record the availability reference for use in the constitutive deed.
required_dossiers: Declaration of distinctive feature/compliant use of abbreviation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is refused, file a new name variant with a written explanation and reservation confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of constitutive deed and partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary or all partners by private signature
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the constitutive deed and SCSp partnership agreement, containing contributions, allocation, management, capital (if any), and the registered office address. For a private deed, each signatory must initial every page and the signature must be notarially legalized if the LBR requires it; otherwise the deed is signed before a notary for authenticity.
required_dossiers: Identity documents (passport/ID) of general and limited partners
Consent and sample signature of officers/managers
Letter of occupancy consent from registered office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the notary or partner objects to a legal ambiguity, amend the deed, reinitial the pages, and resubmit to the notary or, if private deed, provide a notarized transcription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of constitutive deed with the RCSL / Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL) – MyLBR electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic registration application to the LBR, attach an authenticated copy of the constitutive deed, and pay the filing fee (presently EUR 84). The LBR will issue an RCSL registration certificate, which constitutes the SCSp’s identity number for legal relations.
required_dossiers: Record of general partner and managers (name, DOB, nationality)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a regularization notice, submit a rectification petition and amended deed within the 15-day legal period to avoid cancellation of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of beneficial ownership information with the RBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCSL registration, complete the RBE declaration inside the LBR IT system, identifying every beneficial owner (natural person controlling or economically benefiting from the SCSp). Submit the controls as well as the ownership/control percentage of limited and general partners.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify RBE data by filing a correction update; late omissions are subject to administrative fines set in the Law of 13 January 2019.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for mandatory tax, VAT and social security obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Administration de l’enregistrement et des domaines (AED), Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply through guichet.lu for a direct tax number, VAT number (if making taxable supplies of jewelry/watches), and employer/administrative registration. The SCSp is generally transparent; the general partner may need to declare amounts attributable. Confirm whether VAT registration is required under EU e-commerce thresholds for cross-border distance sales.
required_dossiers: Bank account details (optional for VAT registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax authorities reject VAT or direct tax numbers, submit an updated EORI declaration and coordinate with the ACD divisional office to correct tax coding.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Enterprise Legalization (Direction de la légalisation des entreprises)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d’établissement (establishment authorization) if physical premises are used; no sectoral license is required for online sales of jewelry/watches

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required for pure online retail activity; no industrial facility or waste generation exceeding exemption thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; storage and sales activities are subject only to general municipal health and waste segregation rules under the Grand-Ducal Regulation on waste

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety conformity and building clearance are required for any office/warehouse under the Ministry of the Interior and municipal authority; no industrial workplace licensing is applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT/indirect taxes; central digital portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first obtain a Luxembourg national identification number (numéro d'identification) via the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) through MyGuichet if it has a registered establishment, branch, or fixed place of business. For VAT purposes, the entity must register with the AEDT VAT department (Service TVA) using the dedicated registration form and supporting corporate documents, proof of identity of managers/partners, a power of attorney if represented, and evidence of Luxembourg VAT nexus. A non-established foreign supplier with no permanent establishment but making taxable Luxembourg supplies may register directly for a VAT number through the VAT department or use the EU OSS scheme for distance sales. An SCSp is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes but is separately identifiable and registerable for VAT collection obligations when it carries on an economic activity in its own name.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; the SCSp is a special limited partnership with no legal personality and is statutorily tax-transparent; Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax are imposed at the partner level; for VAT purposes the SCSp is treated as a taxable person to the extent it conducts independent economic activity, with the partnership itself liable for VAT remittance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or elective entity classification regime exists in Luxembourg. The pass-through characterization of an SCSp is mandatory and derived from partnership law and direct tax law. Luxembourg has implemented EU hybrid mismatch rules via the law of 27 December 2019; where a foreign jurisdiction treats the SCSp as taxable, Luxembourg may adjust or deny deduction rights to prevent double non-taxation. Partners may submit supporting declarations and self-certifications under the hybrid mismatch framework, but no general election is available to convert the SCSp into a corporate taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Law (loi TVA) pursuant to EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover threshold for established Luxembourg small enterprises; EUR 10,000 EU-wide distance-sales threshold for cross-border B2C e-commerce; non-established foreign suppliers have no registration exemption and must register/use OSS from their first taxable supply in Luxembourg
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control API is currently mandatory in Luxembourg. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2G contracts via PEPPOL; B2B e-invoicing is permitted and accepted. EU ViDA reforms are expected to introduce structured e-invoicing and digital reporting in the future. The OSS/IOSS regimes are available for distance sales and import consignments, requiring indirect registration through the Luxembourg HMRC-comparable portal rather than domestic real-time clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to goods physically exported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union, provided the export is evidenced by a customs export declaration and transport documentation. For online sales of jewelry, watches, and fashion accessories to non-EU consumers, zero-rating is claimable when the goods are dispatched or transported by the supplier or on its behalf out of the EU. B2B services supplied to non-EU customers are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (place-of-supply rule) and are not treated as zero-rated exports; supporting evidence of customer status and place of establishment is required. The 0% rate is not conditional on FX repatriation under Luxembourg exchange control, but documentary proof of payment strengthens the audit file.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice and sales order or contract
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate / proof of payment from the non-EU buyer
Packing list for the exported goods
Certificate of Origin or any preferential origin documentation where applicable
Delivery or handover evidence showing physical departure from the EU
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively deny zero-rating and reassess Luxembourg VAT at 17% on the full transaction value if export proof is missing, incomplete, or fraudulent. Interest on unpaid VAT accrues from the due date, and administrative penalties can be imposed for incorrect declarations, generally up to 10% of the tax for good-faith errors and higher for gross negligence. Deliberate fraud, forgery of customs or transport evidence, or abusive exploitation of the zero-rating regime may trigger criminal fines up to EUR 12,500 plus imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years under Luxembourg criminal law, joint and several liability of managing partners, and full clawback of any input VAT credits claimed in connection with the export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating as the national central bank within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) under the European Central Bank (ECB) umbrella; prudential and AML/CFT supervision of credit institutions, payment institutions and electronic money institutions is vested in the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); the Cellule de Renseignements Financiers (CRF) is the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit receiving suspicious transaction reports; the Ministry of Finance coordinates implementation of EU restrictive measures and sanctions. There is no separate foreign-exchange administration authority in Luxembourg; the BCL executes Eurosystem monetary policy and manages official reserves only and does not issue exchange-control licences.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies under Articles 63-66 TFEU and Luxembourg law: the euro is freely convertible, and no exchange-control authorisation is required for current-account payments (supplier invoices, fees, royalties) or capital-account transactions (equity contributions to the SCSp, partner loans, dividends or liquidation distributions to non-resident partners). Transfer of profits and return of capital are unrestricted, subject solely to AML/KYC documentation and CRF reporting obligations. USD, GBP and CHF proceeds received from Stripe and PayPal settlements may be converted to EUR freely at any Luxembourg-regulated credit institution without BCL notification. Practical barriers are documentary only: source-of-funds evidence for partner capital injections above EUR 10,000, contractual support for every trade disbursement, and sanctions screening of counterparties. No limitation exists on holding multiple currency accounts or maintaining offshore balances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio and no surrender requirement for export or e-commerce receipts. A Luxembourg SCSp may lawfully retain 100% of foreign-currency revenue indefinitely, hold USD/GBP/CHF sub-accounts, and hedge at its discretion. For treasury discipline, the blueprint recommends an internal policy of converting PSP settlements to EUR within five business days and capping aggregate open foreign-currency exposure at 25% of projected monthly operating costs, unless the partnership's FX risk policy expressly permits a higher natural hedge.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Operational Account (EUR/USD/GBP) with dedicated merchant settlement collection account and capital escrow sub-account
Operational Current Account with escrow-capable sub-account for partner capital contributions and e-commerce settlement rail
Operational Account with trade finance module (Commercial Letter of Credit issuance, SWIFT MT103/MT700 channels, documentary collections)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess/BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (domestic payroll, opex and secondary settlement rail)
Operational Account (SME e-commerce corridor, SEPA-only clearing)
Operational Account (corridor banking for Italian and European luxury supply chain, trade finance capabilities)
Capital Escrow Account (private-banking-grade custody for partner capital contributions and wealth management)
Private Wealth Account (holding only; not suitable as treasury or settlement rail for e-commerce)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: B+ (High as auxiliary settlement rail; Low-Medium as sole treasury bank). Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions and PSP frameworks suitable for the SCSp include: (i) MANGOPAY S.A., a CSSF-authorised EMI purpose-built for marketplace and platform payouts, well suited to splitting Stripe/PayPal merchant flows, inventory purchases and logistics fee disbursements; (ii) PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. & Cie, S.C.A., a CSSF-supervised credit institution that serves as the legal PSP entity for PayPal merchant settlement in the EEA; (iii) passported EU/EEA EMIs such as Wise Europe S.A. (Belgian NBB supervision), Airwallex (Dutch DNB supervision) and Revolut Payments UAB (Lithuanian BoL supervision), usable for low-cost FX conversion but not CSSF-authorised and without Luxembourg deposit guarantee coverage. Legal constraints under the Luxembourg Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services (PSD2 transposition): e-money balances are not deposits and are not protected by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme (Fonds de Garantie Déposants Luxembourg); EMIs cannot grant credit; and the merchant bears insolvency risk of the EMI. Mitigation protocol: cap aggregate EMI and PSP-pool balances at EUR 100,000, activate automatic daily sweeps to a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank account, and route all supplier disbursements above EUR 25,000 exclusively through bank rails (SEPA or SWIFT MT103).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law (AML Law of 12 November 2004 as amended and CSSF Regulation 12-02) does not statutorily require an in-person KYC interview, provided identity is verified through a qualified electronic signature under eIDAS, certified/notarised identity documents, or a supervised introduction by a CSSF-regulated professional (bank, MiFID investment firm, lawyer, or approved statutory auditor). In practice, all universal banks in Luxembourg (BGL BNP Paribas, BIL, Société Générale) enforce a de facto physical meeting for the General Partner's managing director or the SCSp's authorised signatory at account opening. Remote opening is accepted only when (i) the SCSp is introduced by a Luxembourg law firm or audit firm under the professional introduction exemption, (ii) a Luxembourg notary authenticates the partnership agreement and the power of attorney, and (iii) the bank's compliance officer completes an audio/video interview with e-signature validation. Limited Partners (passive investors) are never required to appear; their identification is completed via certified passport copies and signed UBO declarations. Lead times: physical opening one to two weeks; remote opening via professional introduction three to five weeks. Recommendation: appoint a Luxembourg corporate services provider (member of ABBL or INPLP network) to sponsor account opening and maintain a permanent KYC dossier (cabinet KYC) for future banking relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp pass-through opacity: a partnership with no separate legal personality held by non-resident partners triggers 'concealment of beneficial ownership' alerts under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the Luxembourg AML law of 12 November 2004, which classify the SCSp, its General Partner and every Limited Partner as distinct clients for identification purposes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier bundle required: (i) fully executed partnership agreement (contrat de société) with a complete schedule of partners; (ii) RCS non-inscription certificate evidencing the absence of legal personality and identifying the General Partner; (iii) if the GP is a Luxembourg SARL, its Articles of Association, registered UBO file and good-standing certificate; (iv) executed UBO declarations (CSSF Form 12-02) for every partner holding 25% or more or exercising effective control; (v) a legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat confirming tax transparency, treaty eligibility and absence of disqualification of the GP; (vi) 24-month source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for each contributing partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Luxury goods trade risk: jewelry and fine watches are internationally flagged for trade-based money laundering (over/under-invoicing, smuggling, acquisition of portable high-value assets with illicit funds), aggravated by cross-border e-commerce delivery to private consumers in medium-risk corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier bundle required: (i) supplier-side master agreements and proforma invoices from authorised watch and jewelry brands or their authorised distributors; (ii) independent provenance and appraisal certificates (e.g., Gemological Institute of America or Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry) for any item with unit value above EUR 10,000; (iii) serial-numbered inventory ledger with photographs and chain-of-custody records; (iv) EU customs declarations (SAD) and export documentation evidencing declared values; (v) transfer-pricing and margin documentation for wholesale vs retail channel sales; (vi) insured logistics contracts (DHL, FedEx, UPS) with proof-of-delivery records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party PSP settlement dependency: concentration of revenue through Stripe and PayPal raises bank concern about commingled funds, chargeback abuse, inability to trace underlying customer transactions, and potential use of the PSP layer as an alternative to a regulated banking account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier bundle required: (i) executed merchant agreements with Stripe Technology Europe Ltd (Ireland) and PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. & Cie, S.C.A. (Luxembourg); (ii) six months of PSP settlement statements mapping each payout to the Luxembourg operational account; (iii) technical underwriting evidence (3-D Secure 2.0 activation, AVS/CVV verification, velocity rules, device fingerprinting); (iv) written PSP risk policy including rolling reserve set at 5-10% of transaction volume and chargeback provisioning methodology; (v) written undertaking to notify the bank of every new PSP contract within 15 days; (vi) first-party chargeback and dispute logs exported from Stripe Radar and PayPal Resolution Centre.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and high-risk geography exposure: online luxury goods reach more than one hundred destination countries, creating accidental nexus to EU/OFAC-sanctioned jurisdictions (Russia, Belarus, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea) and high-risk last-mile corridors (UAE, GCC), which Luxembourg banks scrutinise during continuous monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier bundle required: (i) active geoblocking and restricted-shipping list applied in PSP settings, aligned with EU restrictive measures implemented by CSSF; (ii) real-time customer screening against EU, OFAC and UN sanctions lists; (iii) internal approval workflow and enhanced KYC for any delivery to high-risk countries; (iv) approved courier and freight-forwarder list to prevent transshipment through sanctioned hubs; (v) signed sanctions compliance policy with quarterly testing and monitoring reports delivered to the bank upon request.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing protocol: (i) partner capital contributions must be wired from the partner's own bank account via SWIFT MT103 to the SCSp's Tier-1 Luxembourg account (e.g., BGL BNP Paribas BIC BGLLLULL), with Field 70 remittance reference 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION LU_SCSP' and the partner name matching the partnership agreement exactly; no BCL or CSSF filing is required for the injection itself. (ii) For USD contributions, the remitting bank should include ICC purpose code 'EQUI' (equity) where applicable, and the receiving bank may hold USD in a sub-account or convert to EUR by standing instruction at spot; source-of-funds documentation is required for any contribution above EUR 10,000. (iii) Partner loans, if used, must be routed with Field 70 'INTERCOMPANY LOAN [date] [loan agreement reference]' and supported by a pre-existing written loan agreement with arm's-length interest (ECB rate plus margin) to prevent tax or AML recharacterisation. (iv) E-commerce inflows from Stripe and PayPal arrive as batched SEPA Credit Transfers or SWIFT credits with merchant descriptor 'SCSp name - ISIC 4791 jewelry', and each settlement must be reconciled against the partnership's revenue ledger monthly. (v) Verification protocol: all inbound credits are matched to the partnership accounts, and unusual deposits are reported to the CRF only when undocumented; capital injections with proper documentation are exempt from STR reporting. Structural rule: partner capital must never commingle with PSP settlement daily balances; the blueprint requires a segregated capital escrow sub-account for all partner contributions until the first audited financial statements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Priority clearing rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for all EUR payments inside SEPA (EU suppliers, customs brokers, logistics, EU customer refunds) with T+1 settlement via Target2; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA and foreign-currency payments (Swiss CHF watch suppliers, US vendors, Asian procurement), each wire referencing the underlying commercial invoice and declared purpose per bank-approved purpose code list; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) for high-value watch procurements above EUR 100,000, issued by the Luxembourg bank at 60-90 days sight, with required documents (commercial invoice, airway bill, insurance certificate, brand authenticity certificate) presented through a confirming bank (e.g., in Switzerland); (iv) Documentary collections (SWIFT MT400/MT420) for mid-size consignments between EUR 20,000 and EUR 100,000 to reduce LC issuance costs; (v) refund and chargeback obligations to Stripe and PayPal funded via SEPA Direct Debit or PSP reserve balances, with the operational account holding a liquidity buffer of at least 15% of monthly gross sales to absorb refund volatility; (vi) FX conversion executed at the Luxembourg bank's treasury desk at spot T+2 rather than via PSP conversion, which carries materially wider spreads; (vii) daily treasury sweep moving balances above EUR 250,000 into a CSSF-compliant low-volatility NAV money-market fund (UCITS) or a term deposit ladder (1-3-6 months), while maintaining repo-eligible liquidity. All outbound wires are screened in real time against CSSF sanction lists, with a release-only-by-compliance workflow enabled.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright deliverable forwards (1M-12M tenors) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with the custodian bank
EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF deliverable forwards for hedging merchant settlement proceeds in GBP and Swiss supplier payables in CHF
EUR/USD FX swaps (TOM/NEXT and standard tenors) for daily liquidity bridging of PSP settlement timing gaps
Vanilla FX options (EUR call/USD put and EUR put/USD call) with upfront premium for asymmetric protection on large USD receivables
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD CCS) for long-term balance-sheet hedging if partner loans or bank debt are denominated in USD

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for exotic emerging-market currencies (TRY, INR, BRL) to hedge treasury exposures from market-expansion corridors, permitted under ISDA 2002 and capped at 10% of gross foreign-currency exposure by internal policy

All hedging contracts are restricted to risk-reduction purposes only; speculative trading is contractually prohibited in the partnership treasury policy, with monthly mark-to-market reporting and a hard value-at-risk limit of EUR 50,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, annex) and statutory audit report if applicable, filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) e-filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of annual accounts and no later than seven months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SCSp, partner approval by 30 June and RCS filing by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered coercive fine for late filing; persistent failure gives the Trade Court power to order judicial dissolution; RCS administrative strike-off and loss of legal standing follow in case of continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial-owner data in the Luxembourg Beneficial Owners Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every calendar year by 31 March, confirming UBO data as at the preceding 31 December; any change in beneficial ownership arising from a partnership-interest transfer must be filed within 30 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and criminal penalties under Luxembourg AML Act for inaccurate or late UBO declarations; the RBE may flag the entity to enforcement authorities, and continued non-compliance can result in court-imposed sanctions and suspension of distribution or voting rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered-office continuity and professional agent renewal confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS/LBR and the appointed Luxembourg registered-office / corporate agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuously required; annual confirmation at the registration anniversary and upon each agent renewal. Any relocation of the registered office must be filed prior to the effective move.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inability to receive legal process, risk of default proceedings; non-renewal by the registered agent without replacement leads to administrative deregistration and strike-off of the SCSp from the RCS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SCSp must appoint an approved Luxembourg statutory auditor when at least two of the following three criteria are exceeded at the balance-sheet date: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million, annual net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and an average workforce of 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for public-interest, credit, insurance, pension, and regulated fund entities, and for any SCSp part of a group required to present consolidated accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as transposed by the Law of 19 December 2020 implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS may be voluntarily adopted for annual accounts and is mandatory for consolidated accounts of entities whose securities are admitted to trading on a regulated market.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must reconcile its partnership register on an annual basis. A transfer of partnership interests or economic ownership is documented in the on-site register before the transfer is recognised; any resulting UBO change is reported to the RBE within 30 days. In every first quarter (by 31 March), the general partner must also use the RBE portal to confirm that the UBO information as at 31 December remains accurate and complete, irrespective of whether a transfer occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book (SCSp: kept respectively as register of partners including limited and general partners, register of the corporate general partner's managers/directors, and minutes of partners' meetings and resolutions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate standard rate in Luxembourg City (17% national corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax; reduced 15% national rate applies on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable income).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp is fiscally transparent, so it is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax or net wealth tax at entity level; profits flow through to partners and are taxed at partner level. For a corporate partner resident in Luxembourg, the participation exemption provides 100% exemption for dividends and capital gains if a 10% holding or a EUR 1.2 million acquisition value threshold is met and a 12-month holding condition applies. An e-commerce trading activity in jewelry/timepieces does not qualify for patent box benefits except for embedded IP; the Luxembourg IP box grants an 80% exemption of net IP income derived from qualifying assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 540/541 – Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des sociétés de personnes (partnership income tax return). Electronic filing is mandatory via MyGuichet.lu or the Luxembourg Tax Administration's eTVA/FTE portal; VAT returns are filed separately on Form 2000 series.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (calendar year for most partnerships, unless a derogatory commercial year-end was approved).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the electronic tax return must be filed by 31 December of the following year (e.g., FY 2024 return due 31 December 2025). Paper filings are generally due by 30 June of the year following the taxable period; an approved extension can be requested through the tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registry number (RCS), legal form (SCSp), registered office address, ELP national tax number, and contact details of the general partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners do not appear as the taxpayer for the Luxembourg return; the SCSp's general partner signs the return and discloses all partners; non-resident partner names, countries of residence, and foreign tax identification numbers are entered in the partner appendix.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross online sales revenues from jewelry and watches, cost of goods sold, transaction fees (Stripe/PayPal), freight, warehousing, marketing and payment processing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Income is computed substantively as a Luxembourg trade; non-resident partners are attributed a share of the Luxembourg taxable income only if a Luxembourg permanent establishment exists through the SCSp's local management activity, otherwise their share may be treated as foreign-source income not taxable in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable profit/loss to each partner based on the partnership agreement and timing of capital contributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The return must state the percentage allocation to every non-resident partner; the Luxembourg tax authorities will use this schedule to issue the relevant partnership allocation certificate and to support any withholding or credit claim in the partner's residence state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, prepayments, and any Luxembourg withholding taxes sustained on investment income attributable to the shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner that has received Luxembourg-source interest, royalty or dividend income derived through the SCSp may attach the corresponding Luxembourg tax-residence certificate and claim a refund under the applicable double tax treaty; the partner's foreign TIN and treaty article reference must be completed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Net wealth and exonerated assets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration required only if the SCSp is used for a determined economic activity that creates a Luxembourg permanent establishment and if the undertaking is considered to be a corporate-type entity for net wealth tax purposes; normally left at zero for transparent SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should be aware that their share of the SCSp's assets may be subject to Luxembourg net wealth tax if those assets are part of a Luxembourg permanent establishment and the partner is a corporate entity; otherwise, no declaration is made.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an ex officio tax assessment and an administrative late-filing penalty of 10% of the tax due, with a minimum fine of EUR 250. Late-payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum). Intentional non-filing or dissimulation of income is punished as tax fraud with criminal fines up to EUR 50,000 and/or imprisonment of two months to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on distributions by an SCSp because the partnership is fiscally transparent and distributions are treated as withdrawals of profit by the partners. For comparison, Luxembourg capital companies (S.A./S.à r.l.) apply a statutory dividend withholding tax of 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and the domestic participation exemption if the corporate shareholder holds at least 10% and satisfies the hold-period requirement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief on any Luxembourg-source income attributed through the SCSp, the non-resident partner must: (1) obtain a certificate of tax residence from its own tax authority; (2) provide the Luxembourg tax administration / paying agent with a completed treaty relief request, including the applicable DTA article and a declaration of beneficial ownership; (3) file the refund request with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration within five years of the payment or attribution; (4) retain a copy of the partnership agreement, SCSp registration, and partner allocation schedule for audit purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic Luxembourg withholding tax is 0% on royalties paid to non-residents; under most DTA treaties the rate is 0-5% depending on the type of IP. Interest: domestic withholding tax is generally 0% on interest paid to foreign corporate lenders; country-specific treaty provisions can reduce or eliminate the rate, with an typical 0% result under arm's-length terms; income due to individual resident lenders may be taxed at 15% in limited non-treaty situations.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Luxembourg taxpayer is required to maintain a Local File and Master File when the group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 50,000,000 and the Luxembourg entity's related-party transaction value exceeds EUR 1,000,000. Country-by-Country reporting is mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000. The e-commerce SCSp will be expected to document cross-border intercompany sales commissions, trademark licences, payment processing fees, and warehouse logistic charges at arm's length.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The SCSp must not be a shell or an artificial structure. Although Luxembourg has no offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations applicable to general commercial partnerships, the SCSp must evidence genuine commercial activity: local strategic decision-making, actual storage or contractual logistics, employees or authorised agents, and operational bank accounts handling the jewellery/watch e-commerce revenue. Where substance is absent, the Luxembourg authorities and foreign tax administrations may apply the OECD GAAR and EU ATAD anti-abuse rules to deny treaty benefits, recharacterise the SCSp as a taxable full corporation, or attribute its profits to an alternative permanent establishment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or under-declaration of e-commerce revenue collected through Stripe and PayPal, creation of false invoices for online jewellery and watch sales, concealment of inventory, or diversion of sales receipts to private accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 50,000 and/or imprisonment of 2 months to 5 years; administrative penalty of 10% of the evaded tax and late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; confiscation of illegally obtained proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner/manager of the SCSp is criminally liable if it knowingly signs a false tax return; courts may pierce the corporate veil and hold the manager's personal assets liable for unpaid taxes, seize travel documents, and impose a ban on company management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany margins on jewellery purchases, watch consignment, or trademark royalties outside the arm's-length range, or failing to maintain a Local File and Master File despite exceeding the documentation thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary tax adjustment by the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration plus compensatory interest; a 10% negligence penalty on the under-declared profit; separate administrative fines of up to EUR 25,000 for documentation failures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign distorted intercompany pricing can be jointly liable for the additional tax plus interest; intentional transfer pricing fraud exposes the general partner to criminal penalties and civil restitution; repeated mispricing may support a director disqualification order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp with no physical premises, no personnel, no real purchase and logistics decision-making, and routing online sales through zero-substance structures to exploit tax transparency while relying on tax havens.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and Luxembourg tax-residence certificate; recharacterisation of the SCSp as a fully taxable Luxembourg entity; application of the Luxembourg general anti-abuse rule resulting in additional tax of 25-30% of the reclassified benefit, plus interest and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner may be personally forced to satisfy the recharacterised tax debts if the corporate form is used as a mere veil for personal trading; travel bans and asset freezes can be imposed where the manager is considered the de facto owner of the passive shell income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and file all beneficial owners of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), failure to perform KYC/CDD on the online store's payment clients, or accepting payments from sanctioned jurisdictions while carrying on the jewellery/watch trade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines from EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,000,000 or up to 5% of annual turnover for severe AML breaches; criminal liability for money laundering if the non-filing hides the proceeds of fraud, with potential imprisonment of up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The manager is directly punishable for RBE non-filing and AML failures; personal criminal fines, confiscation of bank balances, and a prohibition from managing corporate entities in Luxembourg can be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing, Ex Officio Assessment and Unlawful Distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeated failure to submit the annual partnership tax return, non-payment of partner-level CIT instalments, or making distributions from the SCSp despite negative distributable equity or pending tax claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Ex officio tax assessment by the Luxembourg authorities; administrative fine of up to EUR 25,000; late-payment interest at 7.2% per annum; directors may be jointly liable for taxes arising from illegal distributions made before the tax debt is settled.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner may be ordered to reimburse the company for distributions made without legal basis; civil and commercial courts can impose a travel ban and extend personal liability to all unpaid taxes and creditors where insolvency was knowingly aggravated.
